assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: System
items.clue: The object, or group of objects, being considered.

items.label: Mass, m
items.clue: The amount of matter in the material being heated, in kilograms.

items.label: Temperature change, ∆θ
items.clue: The final reading on the thermometer minus the starting reading.

items.label: Specific heat capacity, c
items.clue: The energy needed to raise the temperature of one kilogram of a substance by one degree Celsius.

questions.stem: Which statement gives the specification's definition of the specific heat capacity of a substance?

options.text: The amount of energy required to raise the temperature of the whole sample by one degree Celsius.
The amount of energy required to raise the temperature of one kilogram of the substance by one degree Celsius.
The thermal energy stored by one kilogram of the substance at a temperature of one degree Celsius.
The rise in temperature produced when one kilogram of the substance is supplied with one joule.

questions.stem: Which statement gives the definition of power?

options.text: The rate at which energy is transferred or work is done
The total amount of energy that a device transfers
The time that an energy transfer takes to finish
The force that a machine uses to shift a load

questions.explanation: This is the definition in the specification: power is a rate, so an energy and a time are both involved.

questions.stem: Which word equation does the specification give for the energy change when a system's temperature changes?

options.text: change in thermal energy = mass × specific heat capacity × temperature change
change in thermal energy = mass × specific heat capacity ÷ change in temperature
change in thermal energy = mass × specific heat capacity × final temperature
change in thermal energy = specific heat capacity × temperature change

questions.explanation: The specification's wording exactly: all three quantities are multiplied together.

questions.stem: Which word equation for power is given in the specification?

options.text: power = energy transferred x time
power = time taken / energy transferred
power = energy transferred / the time
power = the work done x time taken

questions.explanation: Matches power = (energy transferred)/(time), written in symbols as P = E/t.

questions.stem: A beaker holds 300 g of water at 80 °C. The water is heated until it reaches 100 °C. The specific heat capacity of water is 4200 J/kg °C. What is the change in thermal energy of the water?
questions.explanation: 0.300 kg × 4200 J/kg °C × 20 °C = 25 200 J, with the mass converted to kilograms and ∆θ found by subtraction.

questions.stem: In the equation P = E/t, which units should be used for E and for t?

options.text: energy in newtons and time in seconds
energy in joules and time in seconds
energy in watts and time in seconds
energy in joules and time in hours

questions.explanation: The specification gives energy transferred, E, in joules, J, and time, t, in seconds, s.

questions.stem: Water is heated from 18 °C to 78 °C. Which value should be used for ∆θ in ∆E = m c ∆θ, and why?

options.text: 78 °C, because ∆θ is the temperature that the water reaches.
351 K, because temperatures must be converted into kelvin first.
60 °C, because ∆θ means the change in the temperature.
18 °C, because ∆θ is the temperature the water starts at.

questions.explanation: ∆ means 'change in', so ∆θ = 78 − 18 = 60 °C, in degrees Celsius as the specification states.

questions.stem: An energy transfer of 1 joule per second is equal to a power of:

options.text: 1 joule
60 watts
1 kilowatt
1 watt

questions.explanation: This is the statement in the specification: 1 joule per second is a power of 1 watt.

questions.stem: A 250 g metal block is heated by an immersion heater. The joulemeter shows that 10 000 J has been transferred and the block's temperature rises by 20 °C. What is the specific heat capacity of the metal, in J/kg °C?
A kettle transfers 360 000 J of energy in 180 s. What is its power?
questions.explanation: P = E/t = 360 000 / 180 = 2000 W, that is 2000 joules transferred every second.

questions.stem: Which line gives the units the specification uses for the quantities in ∆E = m c ∆θ?

options.text: ∆E in J, m in kg, c in J/kg °C, ∆θ in °C
∆E in J, m in kg, c in J/kg °C, ∆θ in kelvin
∆E in J, m in kg, c in J per °C, ∆θ in °C
∆E in J, m in g, c in J/g °C, ∆θ in °C

questions.explanation: Exactly the units the specification lists: joules, kilograms, joules per kilogram per degree Celsius, and degrees Celsius.

questions.stem: A crane does 90 000 J of work in 30 s. What is the power of the crane?
questions.explanation: P = W/t = 90 000 / 30 = 3000 W, using power = (work done)/(time).
